Bank borrowings Bank borrowings are analyzed as follows: As of March 31, 2025 2026 RMB RMB (in millions) Current portion: Syndicated loan / revolving credit facility (i)(ii) — 3,900 Short-term other borrowings (i) 22,562 24,324 22,562 28,224 Non-current portion: Syndicated loan / revolving credit facility (ii)(iii) 22,937 — Long-term other borrowings (iii) 26,972 47,450 49,909 47,450 (i) As of March 31, 2025 and 2026, the Company had short-term borrowings from banks which were repayable within one year or on demand and charged interest rates ranging from 0.8 % to 4.8 % and 0.6 % to 9.2 % per annum, respectively. As of March 31, 2025 and 2026, the weighted average interest rate of these borrowings was 2.0 % and 1.5 % per annum, respectively. The borrowings are primarily denominated in RMB. (ii) As of March 31, 2025, the Company had a syndicated loan which was initially entered into with a group of eight lead arrangers. Following the partial repayment of US$ 830 million in January 2025, the size of the syndicated loan was reduced from US$ 4.0 billion to US$ 3.17 billion . In September 2025, the Company amended the loan facility and reduced the pricing terms from Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus 80 basis poin ts to SOFR plus 66 basis points. Effective in November 2025, the facility was restructured as a revolving credit facility with ancillary facility arrangement. The drawdowns are permitted in both U.S. dollars and Hong Kong dollars, and RMB is also permitted for ancillary facility . The expiration date of the facility was extended from May 2028 to September 30, 2028, with an option to further extend to September 30, 2030. The interest rate of the credit facility was 66 basis points over SOFR or Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (“HIBOR”), and the margin will be 81 basis points for the optional extension period. In December 2025, the Company repaid the outstanding balance of US$ 3.17 billion under the revolving credit facility. Certain related floating interest payments are hedged by certain interest rate swap contracts entered into by the Company during the years ended March 31, 2025 and 2026. As of March 31, 2026, the Company had a total outstanding borrowing amount of RMB 3.9 billion under the ancillary facility arrangement by way of short-term loan facilities, and the unutilized commitment of this revolving credit facility was approximately US$ 2.6 billion. (iii) As of March 31, 2025 and 2026, the Company had long-term borrowings from banks with weighted average interest rates of 3.9 % and 2.5 % per annum, respectively. The borrowings are primarily denominated in RMB. Certain other bank borrowings are collateralized by a pledge of certain buildings and property improvements, construction in progress and land use rights in the PRC, receivables and other treasury investments with carrying values of RMB 30,213 million and RMB 19,975 million, as of March 31, 2025 and 2026, respectively. As of March 31, 2026, the Company is in compliance with all covenants in relation to bank borrowings. EXHIBITS 205 i Table of Contents LETTER FROM OUR CHAIRMAN AND OUR CEO Dear Shareholders, Today, we stand at a critical inflection point in the development of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Vast numbers of AI agents are poised to take on an ever-greater share of work in the digital economy, each powered by tokens generated from models. Agents will increasingly serve as the primary interface between humans and the digital world. As we face unprecedented industry transformation and strategic opportunities of this magnitude, Alibaba Group enters a new phase of entrepreneurial innovation and critical investments for the future. In this letter, we would like to share our thinking about the future – our strategic positioning, competitive strengths, and how we intend to capture the next wave of growth. As we enter the AI agent era, AI models and capabilities are being rapidly incorporated into mainstream workplace and business environments, with token consumption surging across industries. We expect the addressable market for companies like Alibaba that provide full-stack AI capabilities is poised to grow exponentially. Against this backdrop, Alibaba's AI has moved beyond the initial investment phase and entered full-scale commercialization. Driven by robust AI demand, our Cloud Intelligence Group’s external revenue growth accelerated to 40% in the final quarter of fiscal 2026, with AI-related products accounting for 30% of this revenue. This reflects AI's role in driving a comprehensive upgrade of Alibaba Cloud's entire business, as its growth engine fully pivots from traditional compute and storage to models, AI compute, and agent services. credit_strengths.text: Alibaba's operating cash flow remains substantial, covering gross interest expense multiple times over and comfortably funding the disclosed dividend and buyback programme. The cash-generative core, spanning commerce and cloud, underpins liquidity even as profitability compresses, and the group retains a large unrestricted cash balance alongside short-term investments that exceed reported debt.

The debt stack is long-dated and predominantly unsecured, with senior notes and convertible notes forming the bulk of borrowings and bank facilities carrying modest weighted-average rates. The restructured revolving credit facility was repaid and remains largely undrawn, leaving meaningful committed headroom and no near-term refinancing wall.

key_risks.text: Operating income fell sharply year on year as the group invests heavily in AI infrastructure and cloud capacity, compressing operating margin well below the sector median. If these investments do not convert into durable revenue, internal cash generation could weaken further, narrowing the cushion available for debt service and shareholder returns.

The debt note discloses that certain bank borrowings are collateralised by pledges over buildings, land use rights, receivables and treasury investments, and that short-term borrowings carry rates ranging up to the high single digits. A portion of the asset base is therefore encumbered, and floating-rate exposure is only partially hedged.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Gross leverage sits modestly above the sector median, but net leverage is far lower once cash and short-term investments are applied, placing the group in a net cash position on the broader definition. Interest coverage remains adequate, though it has thinned as operating income declined, and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal.

Operating cash flow covers reported debt by a comfortable margin, and the current ratio exceeds the sector median, indicating solid near-term liquidity. However, the absence of a capex tag prevents a clean free-cash-flow calculation, so the true call on cash from AI and cloud investment cannot be fully quantified from the bundle.

overall_credit_view.text: We view Alibaba's credit profile as strong, supported by a net cash position, long-dated unsecured debt and robust operating cash flow. The main pressure point is the sharp earnings decline tied to AI and cloud investment, which has pushed leverage above the sector median and reduced interest coverage headroom.

Our forward view is that debt service remains comfortably manageable, provided AI commercialisation sustains revenue momentum and investment spending does not outpace internal cash generation. Shareholder distributions absorb a meaningful share of operating cash flow, so any further earnings erosion would warrant closer monitoring of the balance between returns and reinvestment.

credit_strengths.text: 阿里巴巴的經營現金流依然龐大，足以覆蓋總利息支出數倍，並能輕鬆為已披露的股息及回購計劃提供資金。即使盈利能力受壓，涵蓋商務及雲業務的現金生成核心仍支撐流動性，而集團持有大量未受限現金餘額，連同短期投資，均超過所報告債務。
債務結構屬長期，且以無抵押為主，高級票據及可轉換票據構成借款的大部分，而銀行融資的加權平均利率溫和。經重組的循環信貸融資已償還，且大部分仍未提取，留下有意義的已承諾餘額，並無近期再融資牆。

key_risks.text: 經營收入按年大幅下降，因集團對人工智能基礎設施及雲容量作出重大投資，令經營利潤率受壓，遠低於行業中位數。若該等投資未能轉化為持久收入，內部現金生成可能進一步減弱，收窄可用於償債及股東回報的緩衝。
債務附註披露，若干銀行借款以樓宇、土地使用權、應收款項及庫務投資的質押作為抵押，而短期借款的利率最高達高單位數。因此，部分資產基礎已被抵押，而浮動利率風險僅獲部分對沖。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 總槓桿略高於行業中位數，但一旦計入現金及短期投資，淨槓桿遠低，令集團按較廣泛定義處於淨現金狀況。利息覆蓋率仍然充足，儘管隨經營收入下降而收窄，而指示性財務風險狀況為極低。
經營現金流以舒適的幅度覆蓋所報告債務，而流動比率高於行業中位數，顯示近期流動性穩健。然而，缺乏資本開支標籤，無法進行清晰的自由現金流計算，因此人工智能及雲投資對現金的真實需求無法從資料包中完全量化。

overall_credit_view.text: 我們認為阿里巴巴的信用狀況強勁，受淨現金狀況、長期無抵押債務及穩健經營現金流支撐。主要壓力點是與人工智能及雲投資相關的盈利急劇下降，已將槓桿推高至行業中位數以上，並減少利息覆蓋率緩衝。
我們的前瞻觀點是，只要人工智能商業化維持收入動力，且投資支出不超過內部現金生成，債務償付仍可輕鬆管理。股東分派佔經營現金流的相當比例，因此任何進一步盈利侵蝕，均值得更密切監察回報與再投資之間的平衡。
